pr.title: Stop storing a special inner body for the coroutine by-move body for async closures
pr.description:
...and instead, just synthesize an item which is treated mostly normally by the MIR pipeline.

This PR does a few things:
* We synthesize a new `DefId` for the by-move body of a closure, which has its `mir_built` fed with the output of the `ByMoveBody` MIR transformation, and some other relevant queries.
* This has the ~~`DefKind::ByMoveBody`~~ `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody`, which we use to distinguish it from "real" bodies (that come from HIR) which need to be borrowck'd. Introduce `TyCtxt::is_synthetic_mir` to skip over `mir_borrowck` which is called by `mir_promoted`; borrowck isn't really possible to make work ATM since it heavily relies being called on a body generated from HIR, and is redundant by the construction of the by-move-body.
* Remove the special `PassManager` hacks for handling the inner `by_move_body` stored within the coroutine's mir body. Instead, this body is fed like a regular MIR body, so it's goes through all of the `tcx.*_mir` stages normally (build -> promoted -> ...etc... -> optimized) ✨.
* Remove the `InstanceKind::ByMoveBody` shim, since now we have a "regular" def id, we can just use `InstanceKind::Item`. This also allows us to remove the corresponding hacks from codegen, such as in `fn_sig_for_fn_abi` ✨.

Notable remarks:
* ~~I know it's kind of weird to be using `DefKind::Closure` here, since it's not a distinct closure but just a new MIR body. I don't believe it really matters, but I could also use a different `DefKind`... maybe one that we could use for synthetic MIR bodies in general?~~ edit: We're doing this now.
pr.author: compiler-errors

processing.reason: The analyzed PR #128506 is an architecture/optimization refactor, not a confirmed semantic bug fix. The historical design stored the async-closure by-move coroutine body inside `CoroutineInfo::by_move_body` and explicitly ran the only two non-`MirPass` stages (`RequiredConstsVisitor` in `mir_promoted`, `MentionedItems` in `inner_optimized_mir`) on that nested body, while `PassManager::run_passes_inner` recursively applied the regular passes. The corrected design synthesizes a `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody` item and runs the normal MIR pipeline, skipping borrowck. The patch evidence shows only pipeline plumbing, `InstanceKind` shim removal, layout-validation removal, and warning-order stderr changes; it does not demonstrate any concrete input on which the old nested-body handling evaluates differently. Constructing a pair with a changed numeric/boolean value would therefore require inventing an arbitrary semantic difference not grounded in the PR, which the task forbids.

analysis.originalLogic: The by-move body for a coroutine-closure was produced by the `ByMoveBody` MIR pass during `mir_built` and stored inside `CoroutineInfo::by_move_body`. `PassManager::run_passes_inner` recursively applied the same pass list to this nested body, and non-`MirPass` work was duplicated manually: `RequiredConstsVisitor` in `mir_promoted` and `MentionedItems` in `inner_optimized_mir`. The by-move body was selected as `InstanceKind::CoroutineKindShim`, with special cases in inlining, ABI/codegen, symbol mangling, and `Validator` checked that the coroutine and by-move coroutine layouts had the same number of variant fields.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Treating the by-move body as an auxiliary body nested in the coroutine rather than as a first-class MIR item: applying the pass manager recursively to it, manually duplicating only some non-`MirPass` stages, and selecting it through `InstanceKind::CoroutineKindShim`. That design can omit or duplicate `RequiredConstsVisitor`/`MentionedItems` work on the secondary body and forces shim special cases throughout `InstanceKind` consumers. The corrected transformation synthesizes a `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody` `DefId` whose `mir_built` is the transformed by-move body, feeds it through the normal `tcx.*_mir` stages, and skips only `mir_borrowck` via `is_synthetic_mir`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs using coroutine-closures/async closures, especially a closure desugared to a coroutine whose closure kind is `Fn` or `FnMut`, with captured upvars, precise-capture projections, and calls through `AsyncFnOnce::call_once`. The by-move body and its drop glue must also be considered for `Fn`/`FnMut` coroutine-closures; `FnOnce` coroutine-closures reuse the original coroutine definition.
analysis.summary: Pipeline refactor for async-closure by-move coroutine bodies: instead of storing a nested `CoroutineInfo::by_move_body` that the pass manager processed ad hoc, synthesize a normal `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody` item with fed `mir_built`. This is an optimization/architecture change, not a confirmed bug fix. It ensures the by-move body traverses the usual MIR stages so `RequiredConstsVisitor` and `MentionedItems` are not forgotten, while `mir_borrowck` is skipped because the body is synthesized from already-borrow-checked MIR. `CoroutineKindShim` and its inline/ABI special cases are removed. No compiler was built and no execution/reproduction is claimed.
analysis.trigger: `needs_coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` is true: `hir::CoroutineKind::Desugared(_, hir::CoroutineSource::Closure)` and `args.as_coroutine().kind_ty().to_opt_closure_kind() != Some(ty::ClosureKind::FnOnce)`. The `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` query then clones the coroutine MIR, applies the by-move capture remapping, creates a `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody`, and feeds its `mir_built` with the transformed body.
preconditions: The body must come from a coroutine-closure desugaring, not an async block or general coroutine.
The closure kind must be `Fn` or `FnMut`; for `FnOnce`, the by-move body is just the original coroutine definition.
The parent coroutine-closure arguments must not reference errors; the code returns the original coroutine `DefId` when `parent_args.references_error()`.
By-move `DefId` synthesis must happen before `definitions.freeze()`, because it creates a new definition during `run_required_analyses`.

The synthetic body must inherit relevant queries from the original coroutine (`generics_of`, `predicates_of`, `param_env`, `type_of`, `codegen_fn_attrs`, etc.) and its `type_of` must be the by-move coroutine type.
Synthetic MIR must skip `mir_borrowck`; only non-synthetic, HIR-derived bodies are borrow-checked.
pitfalls: Do not run `mir_borrowck` on a `SyntheticCoroutineBody`; it is derived from already-borrow-checked MIR and borrowck is not designed for such synthetic bodies.
`RequiredConstsVisitor` is not a regular `MirPass`. If a secondary body is not fed as a normal MIR item, it must be manually run before promotion or required consts can be missed.
`MentionedItems` is also run outside `run_passes` in `inner_optimized_mir`; a nested secondary body can miss it unless manually duplicated.

When replacing `InstanceKind::CoroutineKindShim` with `InstanceKind::Item`, every consumer must be updated; stale shim arms in inlining/cycle detection, ABI, codegen, symbol mangling, or interpreter matching can become unreachable or wrong.

`Validator` previously enforced equality of coroutine and by-move layout variant-field counts. That check was removed because the bodies are no longer paired inside one body; do not infer a layout miscompile merely from changed test diagnostics.
The stderr changes in this patch are diagnostic-order changes (e.g. unused-variable warnings), not evidence of a changed optimization result.
Definition freezing must be delayed until after synthetic by-move `DefId`s are created.
analysis.testStrategy: Use Rust UI/run tests with async closures implementing `Fn`, `FnMut`, and `FnOnce`, including calls through `AsyncFnOnce::call_once`, captured mutable/immutable upvars, precise captures, and drop types so the by-move body and its drop glue are exercised. Inspect both the original coroutine and the synthetic by-move body via MIR dumping (`-Zunpretty=mir` or `-Zdump-mir`), and compile with MIR validation enabled to ensure the normal pipeline accepts both. Check that synthetic bodies do not invoke borrowck, that required consts are collected, and that mentioned items are processed. Add cross-crate tests because `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` is `separate_provide_extern` and its MIR must be encoded/decoded. Treat stderr ordering changes separately from semantic test failures. No compiler was built for this knowledge entry.
